analysis.title: Hiking Into A Bubble: Goldman Finds Only One Fed Cycle Looks Like Today... And It's 1999
key_insights: Goldman's Vickie Chang (Global Markets Daily: Macro Assets in Fed Hiking Cycles) studies how stocks, yields, the curve and the dollar behaved after the first hike in each of nine tightening cycles since 1983. The Fed delivered its first hike since July 2023 about six weeks before Oct 28, 2026, under Chair Kevin Warsh.

Market pricing: roughly three additional hikes, about 100bps of total tightening, per Chang. Goldman economists expect one more hike (Hatzius: 'a second and final hike in December'). In the Reuters poll, 94 of 100 economists expect a hold on Oct 28 and all 100 expect a December hike. Swaps price about 75bp of additional hikes through September 2027.

Goldman splits the nine cycles by size. The 'modest' bucket is 1997 and 2015 (one hike each) and 1999 (175bps). The 'other cycles' are 1983, 1988, 1994, 2004, 2016 and 2022. The average cycle tightened about 260bps over about 13 months. DB's Jim Reid said in September that the market was pricing 95bps over 12 months, against a historical median of 313bps over 15 months.

Equities: the median S&P 500 path troughs within 2 months of the first hike and recovers within 4, in both modest and larger cycles. Six-month returns were flat to positive in every cycle except 1994 and 2022. Twelve-month returns were positive in all cycles except 2022. The 2026 S&P line is tracking this script and sits a few points above its level on the day of the hike.

Yields: in modest cycles the median 2Y yield peaks shortly after the first hike and then drifts lower. In larger cycles it keeps rising for most of a year, about 2 percentage points at the median peak. The 2026 front end looks like the modest template, with the 2Y basically flat since the hike. The 10Y had already pushed through 5% (highest since 2007) before the hike, against a script of +114bps within a year of the first hike (DB).

Curve: 2s10s usually flattens into the first hike and keeps flattening, more so and for longer in larger cycles. In 2026 the curve steepened around the hike and then gave most of it back. Goldman rates strategists say front-end forwards usually peak around the end of hikes and after peak inflation is confirmed, and that flattening tends to stop once forwards peak.
Dollar: the real trade-weighted USD tends to firm into the first hike, with mixed performance afterward. It did best in modest cycles, rising almost 9% over the following two years at the median.

Starting macro backdrop for the three modest cycles: core PCE below 2% in all three. Growth was strong in 1997 and 1999 and weaker in 2015. The labor market was tighter in 1997 and 1999. Shiller P/Es were above the 20x post-war average in 1997 and 2015 and well above it in 1999. Today's Shiller P/E is 41x against 42x in June 1999, and core PCE is 3.0%, double the 1999 level.

Goldman's mapping of 2026: strong labor market and a starting funds rate well above zero (closer to 1997/1999), growth like 2015, equity valuations like 1999, and starting core inflation higher than in all three cycles.

1997 and 2015 were interrupted one-hike cycles. Treasury yields peaked around the hike and fell, and equities initially fell. In 1997 the S&P was up almost 60% two years after the hike. In 2015 it took much longer to regain pre-hike levels and was mostly rangebound. The Fed stopped in 1997 because inflation was contained (then the Asian crisis), and in 2015 because of collapsing oil, China's slowdown, volatility and Brexit.

Goldman's growth/policy shock framework: 1997 had dovish policy shocks plus positive growth shocks. 2015 had dovish policy shocks plus growth worries, so equities struggled longer and did not rally strongly.

1999 template: the Fed hiked after the 1998 insurance cuts into strong growth and high valuations. Yields kept rising for almost a year, the S&P 500 went nowhere, and the tech bubble eventually burst and contributed to the 2001 recession. Chang says the 1999 context of hiking into an ongoing investment boom shares features with today, though the macro imbalances were 'generally less visible now'. Goldman says breadth is at dot-com extremes.

Goldman baseline (a modest number of hikes, growth around potential, gradual inflation relief) sits 'somewhere in between these three historical examples' and implies 'a modestly positive path for equities from here'.

Goldman's three scenarios: (1) 1997 version, the best case, a shorter cycle from faster inflation relief that likely requires oil price relief. (2) 2015 version, a cycle interrupted by growth worries if pockets of financial stress broaden, less friendly for risk assets at first. (3) 1999 version, growth holds and this becomes a more extended tightening driven by the investment boom, raising the risk of a growth downgrade later.

ZeroHedge's own view (not Goldman's): 1999 is the most likely template. The 1997 path needs oil relief, with Brent pushing toward $106 and the US-Iran conflict ongoing. The 2015 path needs the Fed to blink with core inflation at 3%. The market already prices a cycle closer to 1999's 175bps.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's baseline sits between the 1997, 1999 and 2015 examples and implies a modestly positive path for equities. In the 1997 case, faster inflation relief shortens the cycle and gives the best market outcome.
tension_points.bear_case: In the 1999 case, growth holds and the Fed keeps tightening into an investment boom with the Shiller P/E at 41x. Core inflation is 3.0%, above all three modest cycles, and the risk of a growth downgrade rises the longer tightening continues.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Brent staying near $106 would block the 1997 path, which Goldman says likely requires oil price relief; broadening financial stress would shift the path toward 2015.

theme_stances.key_argument: Of the three modest cycles, the one whose macro backdrop best matches 2026 is 1999, a hike into an investment boom with high valuations.
theme_stances.evidence: hiking cycle into an ongoing investment boom shares some obvious features with 1999
